title: Post-8461 governed recovery read-only plans and device generation possession safety

phases.objective: Source-only Hostinger inventory, MCP/runtime schema decision, device generation possession safety, 60 operational cases, and Production log-based NO-GO diagnostic; no provider/Production mutation. Add provider-neutral governed Recovery Orchestrator core and admin-only capability discovery, with no mutating HTTP route or live provider authority.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Internal read-only provider planner and source-only security contracts
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: All unsafe, mismatched, absent or caller-injected authority remains nonexecutable; positive read-only evidence can only create a proposal.
steps: Call bounded Hostinger GET-only inventory with managed token callback and validate exact account binding.
Derive MCP schema recovery classification from one-session runtime identity and both table states.
Verify ECDSA challenge replay resistance and reject caller generation booleans.
Confirm independent live Staging, DB-grants, hardware and Production gates remain open.
Validate 60 Hostinger/MCP/Windows/migration/policy/release operational cases and map their independent live proof.
Classify sanitized Hostinger Production log symptoms and reject upgrades with missing schema, privileges, bootstrap or audit persistence.
assertions: Hostinger database CREATE, Node environment PUT, SSH mutation and Production deploy are never invoked.
No provider credential, secret, or environment value is present in reports.
Unknown or inaccessible schema/DB role never proposes migration execution.
Stale device aliases or ECDSA proof without nonexportable hardware attestation cannot claim RECOVERED.
Zero of the 60 synthetic scenarios can certify Runtime/Production writes or device recovery without external evidence.
Even HTTP 200 and synthetic all-ready log lines cannot authorize Production branch push, DDL, grants, DB creation or deployment.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Windows interactive user logon with delayed DNS, GitHub, Docker Desktop and incomplete Scheduled Tasks
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: All source safety guards fail closed; no native Windows or Production certification is claimed
steps: Inspect exact Windows Task Scheduler, Docker Engine and DNS evidence without mutating Staging or Production
Keep remote Git watcher alive during bounded transport outages without reusing prior exact-head/eligibility receipts
Re-check local Compose health after Docker readiness instead of trusting pre-reboot source certification
Reconcile missing supervisor only through explicit additive approved task installer bound to principal/path/arguments
Verify silent Scheduled Task actions and ten reboot-specific synthetic failure scenarios
Require separate native Windows reboot, device attestation, Staging acceptance and rollback evidence
Use a PowerShell 5.1 child process with per-process ExecutionPolicy for trusted maintenance scripts on restricted hosts, and verify nonzero exits and Task Scheduler readback
Differentiate literal task owner name from canonical SID and reject foreign SID, wrong logon type, malformed actions or multiple task actions; expose read-only diagnostic first
assertions: No Production deploy, credential changes, database DDL, DNS updates or provider mutations are authorized
Stopped local Docker containers cannot inherit a healthy status from stale pre-reboot certification
DNS or Git failure cannot select a stale SHA or authorize an unverified deployment
Silent watcher arguments remain exact and reject injected/unrecognized switches
Ten source-only cold-boot scenarios never constitute live Windows or hardware recovery certification
Direct .ps1 execution blocked by Windows policy never counts as an installation attempt or a recovered supervisor; Group Policy restrictions are not bypassed
A blocked principal/actions installer never modifies the existing watcher; exact SID equality is necessary but not sufficient without logon type, action and checkout validation
